formats.name: Plain text
formats.description: Unstructured text in some encoding (usually UTF-8 today, historically ASCII / Windows-1252 / Latin-1). The most universal interchange format on every operating system.
formats.open_with: TextView opens directly with encoding auto-detection (utf-8 → utf-8-sig → utf-16 → latin-1 → cp1252).

formats.name: Markdown
formats.description: A lightweight markup language designed by John Gruber in 2004 for formatting plain text documents. Renders to HTML; widely used for README files, documentation, blogs, and chat platforms.
formats.open_with: TextView renders Markdown to HTML via Python `markdown`. Toggle source / rendered view with Ctrl+T.
formats.convert: To HTML: `pandoc -f markdown -t html in.md`. To PDF: `pandoc in.md -o out.pdf` (needs LaTeX).

formats.name: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)
formats.description: Lightweight data interchange format, a subset of JavaScript object literal syntax. Native to web APIs and most modern programming languages have built-in parsers.
formats.open_with: TextView shows it with syntax highlighting; F5 runs `python -m json.tool` to validate + pretty-print.

formats.name: YAML (YAML Ain't Markup Language)
formats.description: Human-friendly data serialization standard. Superset of JSON; commonly used for configuration where readability matters more than parse speed.
formats.open_with: Syntax highlighted on open; the renderer treats it as plain text with YAML-aware coloring.

formats.name: TOML (Tom's Obvious Minimal Language)
formats.description: Minimal config language designed to map unambiguously to a hash table. Used by Python's `pyproject.toml`, Rust's `Cargo.toml`, and many newer tools.
formats.open_with: Highlighted on open; F5 validates via Python's `tomllib` and prints JSON.

formats.name: CSV (Comma-Separated Values)
formats.description: Tabular plain-text format with one row per line and fields separated by a delimiter (typically comma; tab = TSV; pipe = PSV). The lingua franca of spreadsheets and lightweight data interchange.
formats.open_with: TextView opens in Table mode with sortable headers, filter bar, live selection stats, and a chart picker. Toggle to source view with Ctrl+T.
formats.convert: To Parquet: `duckdb -c "COPY (FROM 'in.csv') TO 'out.parquet'"`. To JSON: `csvjson in.csv`.

formats.name: HTML (HyperText Markup Language)
formats.description: The markup language of the World Wide Web. Structures content with tags; styled with CSS and animated with JavaScript.
formats.open_with: TextView shows source by default; Ctrl+T flips to a rendered preview using Qt WebEngine.

formats.name: Python source
formats.description: Source code for the Python programming language — interpreted, dynamically typed, with a rich standard library and ecosystem.
formats.open_with: Syntax highlighted by Pygments; F5 runs via the configured interpreter (`Run → Choose Python interpreter…` discovers system / conda / pyenv); Alt+/ inline-completes via the chat panel's LLM.

formats.name: R source
formats.description: Source code for the R statistical programming language. Used for data analysis, statistics, and visualization. R Markdown (.Rmd) interleaves prose with R code chunks that knit to HTML / PDF / Word.
formats.open_with: TextView highlights R via Pygments' S+ lexer and runs `.r` via `Rscript $FILE` on F5. `.Rmd` opens as Markdown.

formats.name: Jupyter Notebook
formats.description: A JSON document that interleaves code cells, markdown cells, and rendered outputs (text, HTML, SVG, PNG, MathJax). The standard for interactive Python (and other kernel) work.
formats.open_with: TextView opens in the embedded notebook viewer/editor — edit cells, hit Run, the kernel auto-starts; outputs render in place and persist on save.
formats.convert: To HTML: `jupyter nbconvert --to html in.ipynb`. To Python: `jupyter nbconvert --to script`.

formats.name: PDF (Portable Document Format)
formats.description: ISO 32000 fixed-layout document format. Embeds fonts, vector graphics, raster images, forms, annotations, and (optionally) JavaScript. Designed to look identical on every device.
formats.open_with: TextView renders PDFs page-by-page via QPdfView with text search, link-click navigation, and copy-as-text. Toggle to extracted-text view.
formats.convert: To text: `pdftotext in.pdf out.txt`. To images: `pdftoppm -png in.pdf prefix`.

formats.name: Microsoft Word document (Office Open XML)
formats.description: Office Open XML word-processing document. A ZIP archive containing XML parts (document.xml, styles.xml, …) plus embedded media. Replaces the legacy `.doc` format.
formats.open_with: TextView extracts the body via Mammoth, preserving headings, lists, tables, and inline images, then renders it as themed HTML. Source toggle shows the extracted plain text.
formats.convert: To Markdown: `pandoc in.docx -t gfm`. To PDF: `pandoc in.docx -o out.pdf` or LibreOffice `--convert-to pdf`.

formats.name: EPUB (electronic publication)
formats.description: Open ebook standard from the IDPF / W3C. ZIP container holding XHTML content, CSS, images, and metadata, with a spine ordering the reading flow.
formats.open_with: TextView extracts each chapter's text via `ebooklib` and concatenates into a continuous reading view.
formats.convert: To MOBI / AZW: Calibre `ebook-convert in.epub out.mobi`.

formats.name: PNG (Portable Network Graphics)
formats.description: Lossless raster image format with 8/16-bit per-channel RGB(A), palette-indexed, and grayscale modes. Successor to GIF for static images; widely supported in browsers and tooling.
formats.open_with: TextView's image viewer with brightness / contrast / saturation / gamma sliders, eyedropper, crop, and RGB histogram.

formats.name: JPEG
formats.description: Lossy raster image format optimized for photographs. DCT-based compression; quality is tunable. Embeds EXIF metadata (camera model, exposure, GPS) commonly read by digital cameras.
formats.open_with: TextView's image viewer + EXIF metadata panel (Ctrl+I) — camera model, exposure, GPS coordinates, capture time.

formats.name: WebP
formats.description: Google's modern image format. Supports both lossy (VP8) and lossless (VP8L) compression, plus animation (a smaller alternative to GIF) and alpha.
formats.open_with: Static and animated WebP both supported; multi-frame animations get a frame navigator in the image dock.

formats.name: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics)
formats.description: XML-based vector image format. Resolution-independent; supports CSS, animation, gradients, filters. Native to browsers and most modern design tools.
formats.open_with: Rasterized for display via Qt's image reader; raw XML viewable by toggling source view.

formats.name: TIFF (Tagged Image File Format)
formats.description: Flexible raster format supporting multiple compressions (LZW, ZIP, JPEG), multiple pages per file, layers, alpha, and 16/32-bit depth. Common in publishing, scientific imaging, and GIS.
formats.open_with: Multi-page TIFF supported with a page navigator; high-bit-depth images displayed via Pillow.

formats.name: MP4 (MPEG-4 Part 14)
formats.description: ISO/IEC 14496-14 container for video, audio, subtitles, and metadata. Most common consumer video format; usually pairs H.264 or H.265 video with AAC audio.
formats.open_with: TextView plays video files via Qt's QMediaPlayer with transport bar (play / pause, seek slider, mute, volume). Codec coverage depends on the host's Qt+FFmpeg build.

formats.name: MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer III)
formats.magic_bytes: ID3 (with ID3 tag) or \xff\xfb (raw MPEG frame)
formats.description: Lossy audio compression format that defined consumer digital audio in the 1990s–2000s. Patents have expired; tooling is universal.

formats.name: WAV (Waveform Audio File Format)
formats.description: Microsoft / IBM uncompressed audio container. Stores PCM samples directly; large file sizes but lossless and trivial to process.

formats.name: FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec)
formats.description: Open-source lossless audio compression. Typically 50–60% the size of equivalent WAV, with bit-perfect reconstruction. Common for archival rips and audiophile distribution.

formats.name: ZIP archive
formats.description: Phil Katz's archive format from 1989. The container under the hood for many modern document formats (Office Open XML, EPUB, ODF, JAR, APK, Python wheels, browser extensions).
formats.open_with: TextView's unknown-file inspector identifies the archive and shows hex preview. Use `unzip -l` for contents.

formats.name: Gzip-compressed tar archive
formats.description: POSIX tar archive (uncompressed sequential file concatenation) wrapped in Gzip. Standard for source distribution on Unix-like systems.
formats.open_with: Use `tar -tzf in.tar.gz` to list, `tar -xzf in.tar.gz` to extract.

formats.name: Apache Parquet
formats.description: Columnar storage format for analytical workloads. Per-column compression and metadata in a footer; the standard interchange format for data lakes.
use_cases: Storing analytics tables in S3 / data lakes
Interchange between Spark / Dask / DuckDB / pandas
formats.open_with: TextView's unknown-file inspector identifies it via the PAR1 magic. Use `pandas.read_parquet('file')` or `duckdb` to inspect rows.

formats.name: HDF5 (Hierarchical Data Format 5)
formats.description: Self-describing binary format for large numerical datasets. Hierarchical structure (groups + datasets) with chunked storage, compression, and partial I/O. Standard in scientific computing.
formats.open_with: Inspector shows magic-byte detection. Inspect contents with `h5py.File(path, 'r')` or `h5dump -H file.h5`.

formats.name: SQLite database
formats.description: Embedded relational database in a single file. Most-deployed database in the world (every browser, OS, mobile app). Full SQL, transactional, zero-config.
formats.open_with: Inspector identifies via magic bytes. `sqlite3 file.db` for an interactive prompt; `sqlite3 file.db .schema` to dump schema.

formats.name: Python Pickle
formats.description: Python's native serialization format. Can serialize arbitrary objects, including code references — which means **loading an untrusted pickle is equivalent to executing arbitrary code**.
use_cases: ML model checkpoints (legacy scikit-learn / PyTorch state_dict)
formats.open_with: TextView's inspector flags the protocol byte. **Never `pickle.load` an untrusted file.** Use `pickletools.dis(open('f.pkl', 'rb'))` to inspect bytecode without executing.

formats.name: STL (stereolithography)
formats.description: 3D mesh format from 3D Systems (1987). Stores surface geometry as a list of triangles (vertices + normals); no color, texture, or hierarchy. The lingua franca of 3D printing.

formats.name: glTF (GL Transmission Format)
formats.description: Khronos's 'JPEG of 3D' — JSON-based scene description with PBR materials, animations, and skins. Binary variant `.glb` packs everything into a single file. Native to modern game engines and AR/VR.

formats.name: GeoJSON
formats.description: JSON-based format for geographic data (Points, Lines, Polygons, FeatureCollections). RFC 7946. Native to most web mapping APIs (Mapbox, Leaflet, deck.gl).

formats.name: Esri Shapefile
formats.description: Legacy GIS vector format. Each dataset is split across at least three files (.shp = geometry, .shx = index, .dbf = attributes); .prj holds the projection. Still ubiquitous despite better successors (GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf).

formats.name: TrueType / OpenType font
formats.description: Vector font formats with hinting + kerning + ligatures. OpenType extends TrueType with CFF outlines and advanced typographic features. WOFF/WOFF2 are web-compressed variants.

formats.name: ELF (Executable and Linkable Format)
formats.description: Standard binary format for executables, shared libraries, and core dumps on Unix-like systems (Linux, BSDs). Header indicates ABI, ISA, and section layout.

formats.name: Mach-O binary
formats.description: macOS / iOS executable, dylib, and bundle format. Successor to a.out. Universal binaries (`.app/Contents/MacOS/X`) glue multiple architectures together with the `\xca\xfe\xba\xbe` 'fat' header.

formats.name: PEM (Privacy-Enhanced Mail) certificate
formats.description: Base64-encoded DER data wrapped in `-----BEGIN ...-----` headers. The standard text-friendly container for X.509 certificates, RSA / EC keys, and CSRs.
formats.open_with: Inspect with `openssl x509 -in file.pem -text` (cert) or `openssl rsa -in key.pem -text` (private key — handle carefully).

formats.name: ISO 9660 disc image
formats.description: Filesystem image of an optical disc (CD/DVD/Blu-ray). On macOS / Linux, mountable read-only with `hdiutil attach` / `mount -o loop`.

formats.name: Dockerfile
formats.description: Declarative recipe for building OCI container images. A sequence of instructions (`FROM`, `RUN`, `COPY`, `CMD`, …) that Docker / Podman / Buildah execute layer by layer.

formats.name: Makefile
formats.description: Build script for `make`. Each rule has a target, prerequisites, and a recipe (tab-indented commands). GNU make extends POSIX make with pattern rules, functions, and variable expansion.

formats.name: OriginLab project / data
formats.description: Proprietary binary container format from OriginLab (Origin / OriginPro). Houses worksheets, graphs, matrices, layouts, and analysis history. `.opj` is the pre-2018 format; `.opju` (Unicode) is the format Origin has shipped since 2018 — most files encountered today are .opju. The Unicode container is **not** supported by any open-source reader as of 2026.

tools.name: liborigin (Homebrew) → `opj2dat` CLI — OPJ only, no OPJU
originpro Python module (Windows + Origin licence required)

formats.open_with: TextView does **not** read .opj/.opju directly. No cross-platform, pip-installable Python reader exists for OPJU; OPJ has a Homebrew `liborigin` CLI but its third-party Python wrapper isn't on PyPI. Workaround: open the file in Origin (or the free Origin Viewer on Windows) and export the worksheet as CSV / XLSX — TextView reads those natively.
